general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: This course provides basic knowledge of concepts and analytical techniques in international corporate finance, why MNCs make capital expenditures in productive capacity in foreign lands, how to manage cash in MNCs, and how to apply them to international market transactions nowadays. These include the ability to understand the governance of multinational corporations, and their investing, financing, and risk management decisions in a perspective of maximizing the value to their shareholders.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments given by instructors in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU CMS at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

description: This course provides basic knowledge of concepts and analytical techniques in international corporate finance, why MNCs make capital expenditures in productive capacity in foreign lands, how to manage cash in MNCs, and how to apply them to international market transactions nowadays. These include the ability to understand the governance of multinational corporations, and their investing, financing, and risk management decisions in a perspective of maximizing the value to their shareholders.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Discuss the financial operations of a firm within the international environment.
Demonstrate basic understanding of Banking and Money market and types of instruments.
Apply knowledge of interest rate and currency in solving problems in swap operations
Demonstrate basic understanding of the logic and the mechanism of raising the capital, and managing cash and tax by multinational companies
Analyze multinational capital budgeting to enable firms to make informed investment decisions.
Demonstrate the ability to produce a clear oral report and/or academic written report, which follows research ethic, that applies understanding of key concepts in international finance.
Practice ability to interract and cooperate effectively with others in the conduct of business.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: - Individual Attendance: weight 30% of class participation mark Suggestion: Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. Any absence will reduce 0.5 point per time. - Individual Participation in case study discussion sessions. weight 70% of class participation mark Suggestion: Bonus 0.2-0.5 point per correct/good opinion in case study discussion. Lecturer should add mark rubic when providing case study.

assessments.Grading Guide: - Guided by instructor - Example of group assignment: Groups of students are assigned a topic relating to capital budgeting or hedging by diversification or FDI/M&A. Students are expected to write up a professional report that describes their methodology with clear adjustment of their choice of models, findings and discussion and implications. Finally, students need to present their work in class to instructors and other groups. Report are graded to groups and presentation is graded on individual.
